dsa.q: What is the worst-case time complexity of quicksort?
dsa.explain: With consistently bad pivots, quicksort degrades to O(n^2).

dsa.q: Which binary search tree traversal visits nodes in sorted order?
dsa.explain: Inorder (left, node, right) on a BST yields keys in ascending order.

dsa.q: Which data structure does breadth-first search (BFS) use?
dsa.explain: BFS explores level by level, which needs a FIFO queue.

dsa.q: Which data structure does depth-first search (DFS) typically use?
dsa.explain: DFS goes deep first and backtracks, which a stack or the call stack provides.

dsa.q: What is the time complexity of accessing an array element by index?
dsa.explain: Arrays are contiguous, so an index maps directly to a memory address.

dsa.q: Which of these sorting algorithms is stable?
dsa.explain: Merge sort keeps equal elements in their original relative order.

dsa.q: What is the space complexity of merge sort?
dsa.explain: Merge sort needs an auxiliary array proportional to the input size.

dsa.q: Which data structure offers O(1) average-time lookup by key?
dsa.explain: A good hash function gives constant average-time insert and lookup.

dsa.q: What is the height of a balanced binary search tree with n nodes?
dsa.explain: Balancing keeps the height proportional to log n.

dsa.q: In a min-heap, where is the smallest element?
dsa.explain: The heap property puts the minimum at the root.

dsa.q: Which algorithm finds shortest paths in a graph with non-negative edge weights?
dsa.explain: Dijkstra's algorithm greedily expands the closest unvisited vertex.

dsa.q: Which algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree by repeatedly adding the cheapest edge that does not form a cycle?
dsa.explain: Kruskal's sorts edges by weight and uses union-find to avoid cycles.

dsa.q: What is the time complexity of inserting a node at the head of a singly linked list?
dsa.explain: Only a couple of pointers change, regardless of list length.

dsa.q: Which data structure is the natural choice for implementing an undo feature?
dsa.explain: The most recent action must be undone first, which is LIFO order.

dsa.q: How many edges does a tree with n nodes have?
dsa.explain: A connected acyclic graph with n vertices always has n - 1 edges.

dsa.q: Which sorting algorithm performs best on nearly sorted data?
dsa.explain: Insertion sort runs close to O(n) when few elements are out of place.

dsa.q: What is the best-case time complexity of bubble sort with an early-exit flag?
dsa.explain: On already sorted input, one pass with no swaps lets it stop early.

dsa.q: Which data structure is commonly used to implement a priority queue?
dsa.explain: A binary heap gives O(log n) insertion and removal of the top priority.

dsa.q: What is a collision in hashing?
options: Two different keys mapping to the same index
A key that cannot be found
A crash in the hash function
dsa.explain: Collisions occur when distinct keys hash to the same bucket.

dsa.q: Which collision-resolution technique stores colliding keys in a list at the same bucket?
dsa.explain: Separate chaining keeps a linked list (or similar) per bucket.

dsa.q: Topological sorting is defined for which kind of graph?
dsa.explain: A topological order exists only if the directed graph has no cycles.

dsa.q: Which recurrence describes binary search?
dsa.explain: Each step halves the search range using constant work.

dsa.q: Which of these is NOT a linear data structure?
dsa.explain: A tree is hierarchical, not linear.

dsa.q: In a 0-indexed array representation of a binary heap, where is the left child of the node at index i?
dsa.explain: With 0-based indexing, children are at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2.

dsa.q: Which of these algorithms follows the divide and conquer approach?
dsa.explain: Merge sort splits the array, sorts the halves, and merges them.

dsa.q: What is the time complexity of heap sort?
dsa.explain: Building the heap is O(n) and n extractions cost O(log n) each.

dsa.q: Dynamic programming is applicable when a problem has which properties?
dsa.explain: DP stores results of repeated subproblems and builds optimal solutions from them.

dsa.q: What does a greedy algorithm do?
options: Makes the locally best choice at each step
dsa.explain: Greedy algorithms commit to the best-looking option at each stage.

dsa.q: What does "deque" stand for?
dsa.explain: A deque allows insertion and removal at both ends.

dsa.q: Which tree traversal visits the root node first?
dsa.explain: Preorder visits node, then left subtree, then right subtree.

dsa.q: How much space does an adjacency matrix use for a graph with V vertices?
dsa.explain: It stores one entry for every ordered pair of vertices.

dsa.q: What is the best-case time complexity of linear search?
dsa.explain: If the target is the first element, only one comparison is needed.

dsa.q: What balance factors are allowed in an AVL tree?
dsa.explain: AVL trees rebalance whenever a node's subtree heights differ by more than 1.

dsa.q: What commonly causes a stack overflow error?
dsa.explain: Each call adds a frame to the call stack, which has limited size.

dsa.q: Floyd's tortoise and hare technique is used to solve which problem?
options: Detecting a cycle in a linked list
dsa.explain: A slow and a fast pointer will meet if the list contains a cycle.

java.q: Which keyword prevents a class from being subclassed?
java.explain: A final class cannot be extended.

java.q: What is the default value of an int instance variable in Java?
java.explain: Numeric instance fields default to zero.

java.q: Which construct is used to handle exceptions in Java?
java.explain: Code that may fail goes in try, and errors are handled in catch.

java.q: Which interface does ArrayList implement?
java.explain: ArrayList is a resizable-array implementation of the List interface.

java.q: What does the static keyword mean on a method?
options: It runs once at program startup
It is private to the class
It belongs to the class rather than to an instance
java.explain: Static methods are called on the class itself without creating an object.

java.q: Which keyword refers to the current object?
java.explain: this is a reference to the object whose method or constructor is running.

java.q: Which loop is guaranteed to run its body at least once?
java.explain: do-while checks its condition after executing the body.

java.q: Which access modifier gives the widest visibility?
java.explain: public members are accessible from anywhere.

java.q: What is method overloading?
options: Hiding a field in a subclass
Several methods with the same name but different parameters
A subclass replacing a parent method
java.explain: Overloads are resolved at compile time by their parameter lists.

java.q: When does method overriding occur?
options: Two methods in one class share a name
A subclass provides its own implementation of an inherited method
java.explain: Overriding replaces the superclass behavior at runtime.

java.q: Which class is the root of every Java class hierarchy?
java.explain: Every class directly or indirectly extends java.lang.Object.

java.q: Which keyword is used to implement an interface?
java.explain: A class declares the interfaces it fulfills with implements.

java.q: Can a Java class extend more than one class?
options: No, Java allows only single class inheritance
java.explain: Java avoids multiple class inheritance; multiple interfaces are allowed instead.

java.q: Which collection stores key-value pairs?
java.explain: A Map associates each unique key with a value.

java.q: Which keyword is used to create a new object?
java.explain: new allocates memory and calls a constructor.

java.q: How many bits does an int occupy in Java?
java.explain: Java fixes int at 32 bits regardless of platform.

java.q: Which of these is a checked exception?
java.explain: Checked exceptions such as IOException must be caught or declared.

java.q: What does the finally block do?
options: Runs whether or not an exception occurs
Runs only when no exception occurs
Runs only when an exception occurs
java.explain: finally is used for cleanup that must always happen.

java.q: Which statement about Java Strings is true?
options: Strings can be changed in place
java.explain: Operations on a String create a new String instead of modifying it.

java.q: Which method should be used to compare the contents of two Strings?
java.explain: == compares references, while equals() compares character content.

java.q: What can an abstract class contain?
java.explain: Abstract classes may mix unimplemented and implemented methods.

java.q: Which package is imported automatically in every Java file?
java.explain: java.lang holds core classes like String and Object.

java.q: What is the purpose of a constructor?
options: To initialize a newly created object
java.explain: Constructors run when an object is created and set up its state.

java.q: Which of these is NOT a core OOP principle?
java.explain: The four pillars are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

java.q: What does Java garbage collection do?
options: Automatically frees memory of unreachable objects
java.explain: The JVM reclaims heap memory that is no longer referenced.

java.q: Which keyword is used to throw an exception manually?
java.explain: throw raises an exception instance; throws only declares it.

java.q: Which collection keeps insertion order and allows duplicate elements?
java.explain: ArrayList preserves the order elements were added and permits duplicates.

java.q: What is Java bytecode?
options: Platform-independent code executed by the JVM
java.explain: The compiler produces .class files of bytecode that any JVM can run.

java.q: Which keyword is used to declare a constant variable?
java.explain: A final variable can be assigned only once.

java.q: What is autoboxing?
options: Packaging a project into a JAR
Automatic conversion between primitives and their wrapper classes
Converting a String to int only
java.explain: For example, int to Integer happens automatically when needed.

java.q: What does the super keyword refer to?
java.explain: super accesses parent-class members and constructors.

java.q: Which is the correct way to declare and create an int array of size 5?
java.explain: Arrays are created with new and a size in square brackets.

java.q: Which interface defines the natural ordering of objects for sorting?
java.explain: Classes implement Comparable and define compareTo for natural order.

java.q: Which keyword makes a method safe for access by only one thread at a time?
java.explain: synchronized locks the object (or class) while the method executes.

java.q: What does a method declared with return type void return?
java.explain: void methods perform actions without returning a result.

web.q: Which HTML tag defines the largest heading?
web.explain: <h1> is the top-level heading; <h6> is the smallest.

web.q: Which CSS property controls the space outside an element's border?
web.explain: Margin separates an element from its neighbors.

web.q: Which CSS property adds space between content and the border?
web.explain: Padding is the inner space between content and border.

web.q: Which CSS selector targets the element with id "main"?
web.explain: The # symbol selects by id.

web.q: Which CSS selector targets all elements with class "box"?
web.explain: The . symbol selects by class.

web.q: Which JavaScript array method adds an element to the end of an array?
web.explain: push() appends; pop() removes the last element.

web.q: What does the === operator do in JavaScript?
web.explain: Strict equality does not perform type coercion.

web.q: Which HTTP method is typically used to retrieve data?
web.explain: GET requests read a resource without changing it.

web.q: Which HTTP status code means "Not Found"?
web.explain: 404 indicates the requested resource does not exist.

web.q: Which HTTP status code indicates a successful request?
web.explain: 200 OK means the request succeeded.

web.q: Which HTML tag is used to include JavaScript?
web.explain: The <script> element embeds or links JavaScript.

web.q: Which attribute provides alternative text for an image?
web.explain: alt helps screen readers and shows if the image fails to load.

web.q: What does CSS stand for?
web.explain: CSS describes the presentation of HTML documents.

web.q: Which CSS layout module is designed for one-dimensional layouts?
web.explain: Flexbox lays items out in a row or a column; Grid handles two dimensions.

web.q: Which declaration turns an element into a flex container?
web.explain: Setting display to flex enables flexbox for its children.

web.q: Which function converts a JSON string into a JavaScript object?
web.explain: JSON.parse() turns text into a value; stringify does the reverse.

web.q: Which method returns the first element matching a CSS selector?
web.explain: querySelector() accepts any CSS selector and returns the first match.

web.q: Which event fires when a user clicks an element?
web.explain: The click event fires on mouse click or tap.

web.q: What does the async keyword do to a function?
options: Runs it on a separate thread
web.explain: Async functions always return a Promise and allow await inside.

web.q: Which keyword declares a constant in JavaScript?
web.explain: const creates a binding that cannot be reassigned.

web.q: Which of these is a JavaScript data type?
web.explain: JavaScript has Boolean, Number, String, Undefined, Null, Symbol, BigInt, and Object.

web.q: Which HTML5 element represents a block of navigation links?
web.explain: <nav> is a semantic element for major navigation.

web.q: Which tag creates an unordered (bulleted) list?
web.explain: <ul> holds list items shown with bullets by default.

web.q: Which CSS unit is relative to the root element's font size?
web.explain: rem scales with the font size of the html element.

web.q: Which CSS property controls the stacking order of positioned elements?
web.explain: Higher z-index values appear in front of lower ones.

web.q: Which meta tag setting is essential for responsive layouts on mobile?
web.explain: The viewport meta tag controls page width and scaling on mobile devices.

web.q: What is localStorage used for?
options: Storing data in the browser that persists after it closes
web.explain: localStorage keeps key-value strings with no expiry until cleared.

web.q: Which of these is a CSS preprocessor?
web.explain: Sass compiles to plain CSS and adds variables, nesting, and mixins.

web.q: What is the purpose of the HTML <head> element?
options: Holds metadata such as the title and links to styles
web.explain: <head> contains information about the page that is not displayed directly.

web.q: Which JavaScript array method creates a new array by transforming each element?
web.explain: map() returns a new array of the callback results.

web.q: What does position: absolute do in CSS?
options: Positions the element relative to its nearest positioned ancestor
Fixes it to the browser viewport
web.explain: Absolute elements are removed from normal flow and placed using top/left/right/bottom.

web.q: Which protocol secures web traffic with encryption?
web.explain: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS.

web.q: Which HTML5 attribute makes a form field mandatory?
web.explain: The required attribute blocks form submission when the field is empty.

web.q: What is an API in web development?
options: A set of rules that lets programs communicate with each other
web.explain: An Application Programming Interface defines how software components interact.

web.q: What does the defer attribute on a script tag do?
options: Blocks parsing while the script loads
Downloads the script in parallel and runs it after the HTML is parsed
Prevents the script from ever running
Runs the script before any HTML loads
web.explain: Deferred scripts do not block HTML parsing and run in order afterwards.
